stories.title: Apple Support Community forums to close
stories.summary: Apple will permanently shut down its official support forums on November 20. The platform, which originated as Apple Tech Exchange in 1998, has served as a global hub for user-led troubleshooting. The company is currently transitioning the site into read-only mode before the final closure.

stories.title: Newton installs audio guidance for blind residents
stories.summary: Newton has installed the Hear2There app in three city buildings to provide audio navigation for blind and visually impaired visitors. The app offers real-time guidance to entrances, restrooms, and elevators. Former ADA coordinator Jini Fairley noted the technology enhances accessibility that already exists in the city.

stories.title: Digital addiction tool nears usability benchmark
stories.summary: A digital platform designed for substance use disorder treatment achieved a mean usability score of 67.6, narrowly missing the standard benchmark of 68. Researchers noted that while the tool approached usability targets, human factor barriers continue to hinder sustained engagement among adults with lived experience of addiction.

stories.title: User research without patient recruitment
stories.summary: Product teams can evaluate new interfaces, such as discharge instructions, without recruiting patients by using existing data, general population testing, and simulated users. This approach aims to bypass the lengthy recruitment process, though it provides less insight than direct patient interaction. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Museum accessibility and the co-design gap
stories.summary: Museums often rely on Braille panels and tactile reproductions to accommodate blind visitors, but these additions are frequently designed without co-design input. Federica Schneck argues that this approach remains paternalistic, as accessibility is often relegated to a single, secondary room at the end of an exhibition.

stories.title: Co-designed exercise platform for arthritis patients
stories.summary: The Just One Move web platform, co-designed by patients and clinicians, achieved a 4.0 out of 5 usability rating in a study of 37 adults with rheumatoid arthritis. The intervention aims to support movement for those with chronic joint disease through an evidence-informed development process.

stories.title: Redesigning EMS protocols for provider engagement
stories.summary: An agency redesigned its EMS protocols after finding that staff showed little interest in standard documentation. The new version prompted active engagement and questioning from providers during review. The redesign suggests that protocol format influences how effectively information is consumed by those expected to use it.

stories.title: Glastonbury selects £200,000 playground design
stories.summary: Glastonbury chose a new design for Abbey Park’s £200,000 play area based on five criteria, including accessibility and value for money. Residents’ feedback and design quality each accounted for 30 percent of the final score. The project was selected from nine competing proposals.

stories.title: Volvo Co-Pilot wins Red Dot Award
stories.summary: The Integrated Volvo Co-Pilot system has received a Red Dot Award for its in-cab digital experience. The system is designed to provide a seamless interface for operators. The award recognizes the platform's integration within the vehicle's environment.

stories.title: Soft Labor website uses fuzzy typography
stories.summary: Design studio Other Means created the website for cultural publication Soft Labor using SVG typography that remains blurred until a reader engages with it. The design forces users to interact with the text to sharpen the grainy haze. Skimming the content is discouraged by design.

stories.title: Koto updates GoFundMe brand identity
stories.summary: Koto has rebranded GoFundMe around the concept that help adds up, transforming the traditional goal bar into a radiating progress circle. The new identity uses the ring to display specific causes and fundraising data. The shift follows the company's acquisition of the nonprofit platform Classy.

stories.title: Mucho unifies delaCrem gelato brand
stories.summary: Barcelona studio Mucho has unified the identity of Massimo Pignata’s three gelato shops under a single brand. The project aims to connect the artisanal shops without resorting to franchise uniformity. The new look incorporates illustrations to link the stores while maintaining their individual character.

stories.title: Pets retailer evolves sub-brand architecture
stories.summary: Agency HOW+HOW is restructuring the UK’s largest pet retailer into a series of connected sub-brands. The project aims to simplify the experience for owners navigating fragmented veterinary and grooming services. The retailer operates over 450 stores and 400 vet practices across the country.

stories.title: Pentagram designs Hudson Transparencies book
stories.summary: Pentagram has produced a book featuring 58 Victorian educational slides created by naturalist Charles Thomas Hudson. The design uses specific ink density and showthrough techniques to replicate the original plates. The project originated from a social media post regarding the family archive.

stories.title: Jossy’s crackers undergo brand refresh
stories.summary: Jossy’s has updated its brand identity and packaging to compete with larger cracker manufacturers. The company, which produces Lebanese-inspired snacks, sought a bolder visual style to reflect its business ambitions. The new design emphasizes the brand's Mediterranean flavors and authentic bite.

stories.title: Eric Timothy Carlson on Bon Iver’s visual style
stories.summary: Designer Eric Timothy Carlson reflects on the visual identity of Bon Iver’s 2016 album 22, A Million. The album cover features clusters of symbols intended to mirror the production’s digital textures and off-kilter percussion. The design was created to translate the music's synthesisers and autotune into visual form.

stories.title: Film festival logo design trends
stories.summary: A new film festival logo is being cited as an example of original graphic design. The author notes that while few people attend festivals, they serve as a testing ground for visual styles that eventually influence mainstream advertising and cinema. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.summary: Adobe has introduced new AI agents and creative tools across Firefly, Creative Cloud and GenStudio. The company says it aims to empower everyone to create by removing barriers caused by complex software interfaces. Adobe is also integrating its software into third-party ecosystems like Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: Silicon Publishing introduces Prism for data-driven layouts
stories.summary: Silicon Publishing has launched Prism, a platform for automating InDesign templates and data-driven publishing. The tool handles content ranging from financial statements to direct mail. It allows designers to decide where AI helps and where it stays out, which is a novel concept for the industry.

stories.title: Proximal Ventures closes debut fund for AI drug development
stories.summary: Sahir Raoof has raised $27.5 million for Proximal Ventures, a solo VC fund focused on AI-driven drug development infrastructure. Despite a difficult fundraising environment for first-time managers, the firm is betting that AI can transform the services pharmaceutical companies historically outsource to specialized providers.

stories.title: Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million
stories.summary: Oura is acquiring AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for $625 million. The deal follows Oura’s decision to postpone its IPO indefinitely due to market uncertainty. Counsel Health provides chat-based medical advice and physician access, which Oura integrated into its app earlier this year.

stories.title: SRTD Biotech secures €31.5 million for RNA therapies
stories.summary: Germany-based SRTD Biotech has closed a €31.5 million seed round to develop RNA technology that targets specific cells. The funding, led by Mérieux Equity Partners, aims to address the challenge of restricting therapeutic activity to prevent harm to healthy tissue. Investors include several large pharmaceutical venture funds.

stories.title: Alta raises $47.5 million for blockchain compliance
stories.summary: Alta has raised $47.5 million in a Series A round led by Index Ventures, bringing its total funding to $80 million. The company is building a Layer 1 blockchain with programmable compliance. Fintech firm Airwallex serves as both an investor and a key distribution channel for the technology.

stories.title: Private banking fintech Light Frame raises $5.1m
stories.summary: Private banking fintech Light Frame has raised $5.1 million. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: ShareChat parent Mohalla Tech reports FY26 loss
stories.summary: Mohalla Tech, parent of ShareChat and Moj, reported a 78.5 percent increase in net loss to 1,978.4 crore rupees for FY26. Operating revenue rose 40.4 percent to 1,016.3 crore rupees. Management claims it narrowed its EBITDA loss by 58 percent. The loss grew while the performance improved.

stories.title: Froncort.AI secures $2.3 million from Google.org
stories.summary: Healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI received $2.3 million from Google.org to scale its disease surveillance platform. The funding includes cloud credits and technical expertise to develop mAI-NETRA, a tool using satellite imagery and health data to identify infection risks. The startup is one of 15 selected for the program.

stories.title: Spines raises $64 million for AI publishing
stories.summary: Israeli AI company Spines raised $64 million in equity and debt, bringing total investment to $86 million. The platform aims to replace traditional publishing houses by streamlining the production process. The company is challenging the industry by automating the steps that once required a human publisher.

stories.title: Biotech raises $60 million for Alzheimer's research
stories.summary: A biotech company has raised $60 million to pursue oral protein degraders for Alzheimer's. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Canva announces mass layoffs
stories.summary: Canva is cutting 1,271 jobs, or 22 percent of its workforce, in its first mass layoff. CEO Melanie Perkins described the restructuring as a move to address changes in digital content creation. Affected staff face role changes, relocation requirements, or the loss of their positions.

stories.title: Canva's approach to layoffs
stories.summary: Canva is being examined for its handling of recent layoffs, with observers watching to see if the company's treatment of staff aligns with its stated values. The company paired communication with support packages to manage the event. Trust is now being measured against the restructuring process.

stories.title: Canva redundancy package receives mixed feedback
stories.summary: Canva has been praised by some for an unusually generous redundancy package following the decision to cut 22 percent of its workforce. While social media users described the offer as a masterclass, others remain unconvinced. The package provides at least six months of support to affected employees.

stories.title: Managing creative partnerships
stories.summary: Collaboration between specialists like designers and product managers can amplify expertise or lead to complicated negotiations. Seven years of experience at Yandex taught one contributor that expertise does not automatically make teamwork easier. Sometimes, it provides each person with more reasons to believe they are right.

stories.title: AI's impact on graphic design
stories.summary: Generative AI allows posters to be created in seconds, sparking debate about the loss of human creativity and artistic expression. Students at Simpson College hold varying opinions on the convenience of prompts versus the traditional process of brainstorming. Design is now faster than it used to be.

stories.title: Canva cuts 1,271 jobs
stories.summary: Canva is cutting 1,271 jobs in its largest restructuring to date. CEO Melanie Perkins attributed the 22 percent workforce reduction to a decade-first growth slowdown and the rapid adoption of AI. The company is recalibrating its operations to match the changing landscape of digital content creation.

stories.title: The reception of new media
stories.summary: The author reflects on the skepticism surrounding new mediums, noting that even Monet’s work relied on the invention of specific tools. The piece explores the historical tendency to label new creative technologies as cheating. Skepticism is a standard part of the adoption process for new mediums.

stories.title: Adobe targets novice creatives
stories.summary: Adobe is looking to acquire a new generation of users by simplifying image creation through tools like Firefly AI and Adobe Express.
